{{short description|On jumps of upper numbering filtration of the Galois group of a finite Galois extension}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically in [[local class field theory]], the '''Hasse–Arf theorem''' is a result concerning jumps of the [[upper numbering]] filtration of the [[Galois group]] of a finite [[Galois extension]].  A special case of it when the residue fields are finite  was originally proved by [[Helmut Hasse]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hasse |first=Helmut |author-link=Helmut Hasse|year=1930 |title=Führer, Diskriminante und Verzweigungskörper relativ-Abelscher Zahlkörper|language=de| url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/crll.1930.162.169/html |journal=[[Crelle's Journal|J. Reine Angew. Math.]] |volume=162 |pages=169–184 |doi=10.1515/crll.1930.162.169 |mr=1581221|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>H. Hasse, ''Normenresttheorie galoisscher Zahlkörper mit Anwendungen auf Führer und Diskriminante abelscher Zahlkörper'', J. Fac. Sci. Tokyo '''2''' (1934), pp.477&ndash;498.</ref> and the general result was proved by [[Cahit Arf]].<ref>{{cite journal | first=Cahit | last=Arf | author-link=Cahit Arf | title=Untersuchungen über reinverzweigte Erweiterungen diskret bewerteter perfekter Körper | journal=[[Crelle's Journal|J. Reine Angew. Math.]] | volume=181 | year=1939 | pages=1–44 | zbl=0021.20201 | language=German|doi=10.1515/crll.1940.181.1 |mr=0000018}}</ref><ref name=S76/>

==Statement==

===<span id="higherram"></span>Higher ramification groups===
{{main|Ramification group}}
The theorem deals with the upper numbered higher ramification groups of a finite [[abelian extension]] <math>L/K</math>. So assume <math>L/K</math> is a finite Galois extension, and that <math>v_K</math> is a [[Discrete valuation|discrete normalised valuation]] of ''K'', whose [[residue field]] has characteristic ''p''&nbsp;>&nbsp;0, and which admits a unique extension to ''L'', say ''w''.  Denote by <math>v_L</math> the associated normalised valuation ''ew'' of ''L'' and let <math>\scriptstyle{\mathcal{O}}</math> be the [[valuation ring]] of ''L'' under <math>v_L</math>.  Let <math>L/K</math> have [[Galois group]] ''G'' and define the ''s''-th ramification group of <math>L/K</math> for any real ''s''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;&minus;1 by

:<math>G_s(L/K)=\{\sigma\in G\,:\,v_L(\sigma a-a)\geq s+1 \text{ for all }a\in\mathcal{O}\}.</math>

So, for example, ''G''<sub>&minus;1</sub> is the Galois group ''G''.  To pass to the upper numbering one has to define the function ''ψ''<sub>''L''/''K''</sub> which in turn is the inverse of the function ''η''<sub>''L''/''K''</sub> defined by

:<math>\eta_{L/K}(s)=\int_0^s \frac{dx}{|G_0:G_x|}.</math>

The upper numbering of the [[ramification group]]s is then defined by ''G''<sup>''t''</sup>(''L''/''K'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;''G''<sub>''s''</sub>(''L''/''K'') where ''s''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''ψ''<sub>''L''/''K''</sub>(''t'').

These higher ramification groups ''G''<sup>''t''</sup>(''L''/''K'') are defined for any real ''t''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;&minus;1, but since ''v''<sub>''L''</sub> is a discrete valuation, the groups will change in discrete jumps and not continuously. Thus we say that ''t'' is a jump of the filtration {''G''<sup>''t''</sup>(''L''/''K'')&nbsp;:&nbsp;''t''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;&minus;1} if ''G''<sup>''t''</sup>(''L''/''K'')&nbsp;≠&nbsp;''G''<sup>''u''</sup>(''L''/''K'') for any ''u''&nbsp;>&nbsp;''t''.  The Hasse–Arf theorem tells us the arithmetic nature of these jumps.

===Statement of the theorem===
With the above set up of an abelian extension ''L''/''K'', the theorem states that the jumps of the filtration {''G''<sup>''t''</sup>(''L''/''K'')&nbsp;:&nbsp;''t''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;&minus;1} are all [[Integer|rational integers]].<ref name=S76/><ref name=Neu68>Neukirch (1999) Theorem 8.9, p.68</ref>

== Example ==
Suppose ''G'' is cyclic of order <math>p^n</math>, <math>p</math> residue characteristic and <math>G(i)</math> be the subgroup of <math>G</math> of order <math>p^{n-i}</math>. The theorem says that there exist positive integers <math>i_0, i_1, ..., i_{n-1}</math> such that
:<math>G_0 = \cdots = G_{i_0} = G = G^0 = \cdots = G^{i_0}</math>
:<math>G_{i_0 + 1} = \cdots = G_{i_0 + p i_1} = G(1) = G^{i_0 + 1} = \cdots = G^{i_0 + i_1}</math>
:<math>G_{i_0 + p i_1 + 1} = \cdots = G_{i_0 + p i_1 + p^2 i_2} = G(2) = G^{i_0 + i_1 + 1}</math>
:...
:<math>G_{i_0 + p i_1 + \cdots + p^{n-1}i_{n-1} + 1} = 1 = G^{i_0 + \cdots + i_{n-1} + 1}.</math><ref name=S76>Serre (1979) IV.3, p.76</ref>

==Non-abelian extensions==
For non-abelian extensions the jumps in the upper filtration need not be at integers. [[Jean-Pierre Serre]] gave an example of a totally ramified extension with Galois group the [[quaternion]] group <math>Q_8</math> of order 8 with
*<math>G_0 = Q_8</math>
*<math>G_1 = Q_8</math>
*<math>G_2 = \Z/2\Z</math>
*<math>G_3 = \Z/2\Z</math>
*<math>G_4 = 1</math>
The upper numbering then satisfies
*<math>G^n = Q_8 </math> &nbsp; for <math> n \leq 1 </math>
*<math>G^n = \Z/2\Z </math> &nbsp; for <math> 1 < n\leq 3/2 </math>
*<math>G^n = 1 </math> &nbsp; for <math> 3/2 < n </math>
so has a jump at the non-integral value <math>n=3/2</math>.
